findings.title: Three of twelve hotels are in the GCC; possible conflict with the Al Noor restriction, for counsel
findings.quote: | 10 | BlueOrchid Dubai Business Bay | Dubai | United Arab Emirates | | 11 | Orchid Residences Dubai Marina | Dubai | United Arab Emirates | | 12 | BlueOrchid Muscat Qurum | Muscat | Oman |
findings.explanation: The tracker note says Jay thinks it is 'just India hotels', but §4.1 delivers the solution for 'all twelve (12) Properties' and the background says the portfolio is 'in India and the Middle East'. Annexure B puts two hotels in Dubai (UAE) and one in Muscat (Oman); rows 1-9 are Indian. Al Noor §12.2 treats services as 'in the GCC' if they relate to properties located in a GCC state, wherever performed, and Al Noor §1.9 lists both the UAE and Oman. BlueOrchid owns and operates hotels, so it is a Hospitality Business, and AI review analytics looks like 'data analytics' or 'artificial intelligence' services. The Feb 2026 waiver covers only the Seaside SOW in Muscat and expressly excludes any other Hospitality Business in Oman or elsewhere in the GCC, so BlueOrchid Muscat Qurum is not covered. Possible conflict, for counsel: whether guest-review sentiment work falls within the clause is a reading for counsel; the Al Noor §12.4 consent route is in Al Noor's sole discretion.

register_refs.quote: the Supplier undertakes that neither it nor any of its Affiliates shall, during the Restricted Period, directly or indirectly, provide data analytics, artificial intelligence or revenue-management services to any Hospitality Business in the GCC.

For the purposes of Clause 12.1, services are provided "in the GCC" if the Hospitality Business receiving them is headquartered in, or the services relate to properties or operations located in, any state of the GCC, irrespective of where the services are performed.

"GCC" means the member states of the Gulf Cooperation Council, being the United Arab Emirates, the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, the State of Qatar, the State of Kuwait, the Kingdom of Bahrain and the Sultanate of Oman.

The Client may, in its sole discretion, waive the restriction in Clause 12.1 in respect of a specific engagement by written consent signed by an authorised signatory of the Client. Any such waiver shall be limited to its express terms.

This consent is strictly limited to the Seaside SOW. It does not extend to (a) any other services provided to Seaside, including any extension, renewal, change order or follow-on statement of work, unless separately consented to in writing by the Client; (b) any other Hospitality Business, whether in the Sultanate of Oman or elsewhere in the GCC; or (c) any Affiliate of the Supplier.
